text:
Vancouver won in overtime, but Edmonton played the better game, and by a wide margin. The Oilers out-attempted the Canucks 72 to 44 and created 3.68 expected goals to Vancouver's 2.0, which gives them a 78 percent chance of winning if you replay every shot. The Canucks still led 5-2 early in the third period, helped by chances that rarely go in: Jonathan Lekkerimäki's snap shot from a 4 percent look, Max Sasson's backhand and Elias Pettersson's power-play tip-in.

Edmonton's comeback was driven by Evan Bouchard, who finished with three goals and two assists. He scored twice in the first nine minutes of the third's second half, including a wrist shot 24 seconds after Vasily Podkolzin made it 5-3, a chance rated at just 2 percent. Podkolzin then tied it 5-5 on the power play with 43 seconds left in regulation, his second goal of the night from a game-high seven shots. Edmonton's top line of Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl also dominated the shot quality when on the ice, with Draisaitl's group posting 2.46 expected goals for against 0.34 against.

Then came the overtime, and the finish went the other way. Paul Cotter, who had opened the scoring shorthanded in the first, finished a backhand set up by Sasson at 1:59, a 42 percent chance and the best look Vancouver had all night. Tristan Jarry stopped 17 of 23 shots and allowed 4.0 goals more than expected, while Kevin Lankinen's line was 1.32 goals worse than expected. Vancouver took the two points anyway, on the strength of a few shots that went in and one that mattered most.
